content.comment_body: Hello everyone, We've just received our first [article_no] [product_name] for a project. With limited time to experiment, it's already clear this device has great potential. I'm inviting other users to share useful tips and tricks for working with the software and hardware—even if it's information from earlier versions not covered in the official documentation. Here's one to start: HOLDING INSTRUCTION SELECTION In earlier software versions, choosing an instruction (for example, AND) held it selected until you pressed ESC or chose a different one—sometimes inconvenient. Now, in [product_name] V8, when you select an instruction, it's active only until you click on your worksheet. This can also be tricky if you want to insert multiple blocks. To keep your selection held, just double-click the instruction, same as before. This keeps things flexible. (See attached image for details.)

ZOOMING Zooming in and out has been difficult in previous versions. The workflow has improved if you know the shortcuts: ZOOM IN: - Select the object you want to zoom into. - Hold the CTRL key and scroll forward. - The selected object stays centered. ZOOM OUT: - Hold the CTRL key and scroll backward. - The worksheet focus jumps to the first page—don't worry. - If you reach the correct zoom-out level, scroll one more time. - Then scroll forward once to return to your original focus point. This behavior caught us off guard, but it's actually handy when designing circuits—all inputs are on the first page. However, letting go of CTRL means you can't return to your previous focus point. Try out the zoom features and see if they work for you.
Exactly! Double-clicking the instruction keeps your selection held, just like in earlier versions. A small stamp symbol appears next to the block, indicating the current placement mode.

USING WINDOW SPLIT Previous [product_name] versions allowed splitting the worksheet, similar to spreadsheets, but it was mostly useful for viewing. Now, the WINDOW SPLIT function lets you connect instruction blocks over longer distances across the split. Refer to the attached image for guidance.

With workspace splitting, it's possible to work with two or three different [product_name] programs at once. You can directly connect a block from one program to another, and the software handles network inputs/outputs for you. You may edit these network connections as needed. To utilize this function, first set up a network using the NETWORK PROJECT tab.

Splitting the workspace enables you to work with multiple [product_name] programs. Copying and pasting whole programs or sections between different [product_name] instances is straightforward. Simply drag the program tabs across the screen as needed. However, it's unclear how to create multiple pages within a single program. Previously this was under File > Properties, but now it's changed.
[product_name] V8 MESSAGES The attached image demonstrates: - Activating the web server - Multi-language options - Double page setup for the display - Page size settings for the terminal display

SPECIAL MEMORY FLAGS Special memory flags are now easier to select (refer to image). There are several new options. For example, M8 activates during the first scan cycle regardless of inputs, so use it cautiously as it acts as an 'always ON' input initially. Backlight flags can be used to adjust display backlight colors. Be aware: If you use manual backlight control, automatic backlight features are disabled. It's advised to keep at least one flag active for the display to remain well lit.

INTRODUCTION TO [product_name] V8 CONNECTED TO [version_no] PLC The attached image provides steps to set up network connections between [product_name] V8 and a [version_no] PLC (for example, [version_no]). It's straightforward once familiar with the process. Follow the instructions shown in the image, and for connecting [product_name] V7, use similar steps. Anyone is welcome to expand on this guide here or in a dedicated tip.

Hi, follow the instructions in the image: - Maximize your [product_name] window - Save your project - Use the SPLIT function - Click the project name under DIAGRAMS (left panel) - Drag the project into the empty SPLIT workspace Was this helpful?

I wasn't referring to that. When a program has many blocks, I want to create multiple pages for it. I found out how—there's a small icon at the top called "Page Layout." Previously, this was under File > Properties > Page Layout, but now it's accessible via its own icon.
PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: LINK ANALOG INPUT TO TIMER TARGET In [product_name] V8, internal parameter linking is visually represented. The attached image shows an example configuration.
USING COLORS There are now many color options for editing. It's especially helpful to set special flags (such as M8) in different colors for clarity.
WORKING WITH MULTIPLE PAGES IN A PROJECT The attached picture illustrates how to adjust workspace size per page, as well as what another user mentioned earlier (thank you).

SELECTING THE [product_name] VERSION FOR YOUR PROJECT Currently, three versions ([version_no]) are available. Because memory and instruction options differ, it's important to select hardware before starting your design. There are three ways to make this selection, as depicted in the image. Good news: Editing a program from version 6 or 7 in [product_name] V8 still allows opening it in [product_name] V7.1.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to another thread regarding [product_name] V8. If you edit input/output names and the software locks up, refer there. Best regards [user_name]

This may be off-topic, but after inserting a block, the cursor automatically switches to the wiring tool when using ladder diagrams. Is there a way to make it default to the selection tool? It's a bit frustrating when adding several contacts in sequence.
Please refer to the first comment in this thread—your question is answered there.

Your original question is answered, but here's an additional tip: [product_name] is designed primarily for function block diagrams (FBD)—that's its natural usage mode. Ladder diagrams are included as a marketing choice, but they're not as intuitive to work with. Training yourself to use FBD may take practice but is worthwhile in the long run. That's my advice. [user_name]
That's helpful to know. I had to learn the software myself about eight years ago, and only used ladder diagrams; never got around to FBD. Looks like I should have! Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: Users highlight improvements in [product_name] V8 and [product_name] [article_no], particularly regarding instruction selection and window splitting, which reduce previous workflow frustrations. Navigation remains challenging—users mention losing focus when zooming out and uncertainty about multi-page creation. Most feedback is positive, especially about new features such as special memory flags and enhanced network project support, though there are some usability quirks and confusion around less-documented features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect efficient and intuitive programming workflows, easy navigation (including improved zoom and multi-page controls), straightforward handling of multiple blocks, and seamless management of networks and projects within the software.
